_how: Every entry names the FILE, the NOTE and the ROUTE the figure came by (text layer or OCR off the rendered pixels), on the same footing as the four-field rule. A RANGE IS RECORDED AS A RANGE: most policy notes give a band per asset class and not a single number, and collapsing that to one figure here would be this desk choosing the life under cover of a citation. The weighted life a terminal actually needs is derived at rebuild from the property, plant and equipment note's own composition, which is a further sourcing step and is NOT done here.

ADNOCDIST.weighted_not_derivable: THE WEIGHTED LIFE CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THIS DISCLOSURE AND NO FIGURE IS CHOSEN INSTEAD. Unlike ADNOCLS and MODON the composition is NOT the obstacle — note 5 discloses cost, accumulated depreciation and net carrying amount for every one of the five depreciable classes, so a weighting is arithmetically available. WHAT IS MISSING IS A LIFE PER CLASS: the note discloses a RANGE per class, and weighting ranges returns a range. Weighted on the note's own gross cost the disclosed bands give 10.89 years at every low end and 39.87 at every high end — A SPREAD OF 29 YEARS; on net carrying amount 12.20 to 43.41. Buildings alone are 59.9% of gross cost on a band of 15 to 50, so the answer is decided almost entirely by where inside ONE class's range a figure is picked. That pick is this desk choosing a life under cover of a citation (SIGCM clause 1). THE IDENTITY ROUTE THAT WOULD COLLAPSE THE BAND IS CLOSED TWICE OVER AND THE ACCOUNTS SAY SO IN THEIR OWN WORDS. (i) RESIDUAL VALUES: note 3.10 allocates cost 'to their residual values', so the charge is (cost less residual) over life and gross cost over charge OVERSTATES the life by an unknown amount; no residual is disclosed. (ii) THE REASSESSMENT, QUANTIFIED BY THE COMPANY: AED 90,917 thousand of relief in FY2025 on assets carrying AED 5,347,053 thousand — 15.3% of the year's entire charge of 594,222, on 77.7% of the depreciable net book value, applied prospectively — so the FY2025 charge is not the charge that built the accumulated column above it and the identity is broken outright rather than merely biased. On the prior basis the implied life reads 20.51 years against 23.65 as reported and the measured age 10.47 against 12.07: a 15.3% swing in both from an accounting estimate rather than from anything about the assets. THE CHEAP CROSS-CHECK CANNOT ARBITRATE EITHER — the identity's 23.65 years sits inside the 10.89-39.87 band, but a band 29 years wide contains almost any number, so the agreement is worth nothing; the NOTE is the test and the arithmetic corroborates only sometimes. THE ALTERNATIVE BASIS WAS RUN AND IS ALSO CLOSED: 'disclosed_capex' needs a stated maintenance capital figure, and the FY2025 management discussion breaks capital expenditure down by PROJECT TYPE while putting new-station construction and capitalised property maintenance in the SAME category, saying only that 'about 50% of the CAPEX comprised development and construction of new service stations'; the H1 2026 management discussion says 'over 50% represented growth CAPEX' on AED 339 million, a bound over half a year rather than a figure. NEGATIVE SEARCHES ACTUALLY RUN, recorded so the next pass does not repeat them: no maintenance or sustaining capital figure appears in the FY2025 management discussion, the FY2025 or Q1/Q2 2026 results presentations, or the 2025 integrated report. So ADNOCDIST stays on the terminal ratchet WITH THIS REASON. Same disposition as ADNOCLS and MODON, reached by a different route: there the classes could not be split, here they can and the lives inside them are bands.

ADNOCLS.why_the_terminal_refused: MEASURED 04-Sep-2026, and it sharpens the earlier stop rather than repeating it. The rebuild computed maintenance as the WHOLE gross base at 25 years — 303,803 against book property depreciation of 385,487, i.e. 78.8% of it — so terminal free cash flow exceeded terminal profit and the module refused. THE 25-YEAR LIFE IS DISCLOSED FOR TANKERS, NOT FOR THE BASE. Applying one class's life to every class is the life-this-desk-chose error wearing a citation, and it is what produced the refusal.
ADNOCLS.what_the_disclosure_does_support: The gross cost IS disclosed by class and every class has its own disclosed life, so only the vessel line mixes two — hulls at 25 years and dry-docking components at 5 — and only that line is unsplit. The other four classes are 315,131 of 7,595,070 (4.1%), and their depreciation is bounded by their own disclosed ranges to between 23,993 (longest lives) and 61,785 (shortest). Subtracting from the 385,487 the company reports across notes 5 and 6 leaves the vessel line depreciating 323,702 to 361,494, and solving (V-x)/25 + x/5 for that BOUNDS THE DRY-DOCKING COMPONENT TO 2.79%-6.04% OF THE VESSEL LINE. That is arithmetic on the disclosure, not a choice.
ADNOCLS.the_next_step_is_named: Maintenance at the disclosed lives on the GROSS base equals book depreciation on that base by construction, straight-line — which is why the honest charge is near 385,487 rather than 303,803, and why the refusal reverses at any point inside the bound above. WHAT REMAINS is the step from historical to CURRENT cost, and the gap there is NARROWER THAN THIS ENTRY FIRST SAID — see the correction below.

So the accounts are running the machinery column slower than 5%, and note 3/2 names that column 'Machinery' while note 4 columns it 'Machinery & Equipment'. THE DIRECTION IS TOWARD A LONGER LIFE, i.e. toward the study's own committed figure — which is a reason to state it, not to adopt it, because the identity route is contaminated here by exactly the fully-depreciated assets the disclosure quantifies. The DISCLOSED rates are what [R-TERM-01] mandates and what is recorded; the implied life is recorded beside them as a cross-check that does not agree.
SCEM.capitalised_overhaul_and_why_this_is_NOT: Note 3/2 also discloses that 'the company capitalize some expenses related to periodical major overhaul for the production line and add it to the fixed assets', the work done by Relliance Company for Heavy Industries and ASEC. That is maintenance capitalised, which is the shape that left ADNOCLS on the ratchet — but the two are not the same case and the difference is what the note discloses. ADNOCLS discloses a SEPARATE FASTER LIFE for dry-docking (2 to 5 years) inside an unsplit vessel column, so a terminal charging only hull replacement while adding back all book depreciation adds back the amortisation of a cost it never charged, and the life that would split it cannot be derived. SCEM discloses NO second rate: the overhaul enters the fixed assets and is depreciated at the class rate, and every one of note 4's five columns has a disclosed rate covering 100% of the depreciable base. There is no undivided component with a different disclosed life, so there is nothing to refuse for. What it does mean, and it is a caveat rather than a hole: recurring overhaul recycled into a 20-year class understates what the plant actually consumes, which points the SAME way as the harmonic finding — the committed maintenance charge is too small — and is left unquantified because the note does not quantify it.

priced_across_the_disclosed_band_06-09-2.what_this_is: the terminal RE-PRICED through terminal_value.build() on the study's own committed inputs with ONLY the life changed. NOTHING PUBLISHED MOVES; a rebuild is a re-issue with a rebuild ledger and an audit point declared in advance [R-REBUILD-01].

priced_across_the_disclosed_band_06-09-2.no_refusal: terminal_value.build() returns cleanly everywhere in the sourced band: terminal free cash flow stays positive and the implied payout of terminal NOPAT runs 80.6% to 82.2%, well inside [0,1]. The exemplar's refusal condition — maintenance coming in below book depreciation and driving payout above 100% — does not arise here; maintenance is 3.6x to 3.9x book depreciation.
priced_across_the_disclosed_band_06-09-2.direction: the correction LOWERS the value, by 2.4% to 3.5% on the central. SCEM's committed central of 123.27 sits +22.7% ABOVE the latest known price of 100.50 (SUPPLIED_03-09-2026.json), so this moves the answer TOWARD the price. That is stated because the direction has to be reported either way and it is NOT evidence for the correction — nobody may predict which way a rebuild moves a value before running it [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO CORRECTED], and a move toward the price is no more a vindication than a move away from it is an objection.

SCEM.against_the_terminal: The committed terminal is already the sanctioned construction — SCEM is in the census's rebuilt group, not on g x IC — so what is at issue is the LIFE inside it and not the shape around it. Its implied replacement cycle reads 64.0 years in the census's IC/charge column, which is net of a book-D&A add-back and is not comparable to 1/g of 14.3; the life it actually charges maintenance over is 25.889.
SCEM.the_census_reports_this_name_NOT_SOURCED: terminal_census.disclosed_life('SCEM') returns (None, None, None) while the same file's own census prints 'SCEM 25.9 years committed' three tables higher, both from the same study_numbers.json. The reason is exact and it is the failure that resolver's docstring says it was written to prevent, one nesting level deeper: disclosed_life() reads the FIXED path terminal_record.inputs, the widened _walk() that feeds the committed-life table matches the record by its rule='R-TERM-01' stamp wherever it sits, and SCEM commits its record at dcf.terminal_record. ARCC commits at the top level and resolves; SCEM does not. This entry closes the column for SCEM either way, but the resolver is still reading one place and the census two, and any other study committing below the top level reads 'not sourced' the same way.

STC.source: Saudi Telecom Company, AUDITED consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 (Deloitte and Touche & Co.), note 10 property and equipment, immediately under the roll-forward: 'Property and equipment are depreciated using the following estimated useful lives: Buildings 25 - 50 years; Telecommunication network and equipment 3 - 30 years; Other assets 2- 20 years'. Method at note 4.11: 'Depreciation is charged using MAINLY the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of property and equipment, other than land.' Land of SAR 1,996 million is disclosed separately at note 10(1) and is not depreciated; capital work in progress is carried at cost with depreciation commencing when the asset is ready for use (note 4.11), so both leave the depreciable base. Other assets are 'furniture, fixtures, motor vehicles, computers and tools' (note 10(2)).
STC.route: TEXT LAYER, pdftotext -layout. No OCR was needed and the arithmetic is why, not the extractor's confidence: the note 10 movement schedule that supplies the weights was footed 25 ways across BOTH years printed in the FY2025 filing - every class column rolling opening-plus-movements to its printed close in cost and in accumulated depreciation, every row summing across the four classes to its printed total, and net book value reproducing as cost less accumulated by class and in total - ZERO failures, every one to the riyal. The FY2024 filing's own note and the FY2023 filing's own note were footed the same way and also reproduce exactly. The life table itself carries no arithmetic and cannot be footed; a footing page beside it does not certify it, so it is quoted verbatim and nothing is inferred from it that the columns do not support.
STC.L328_condition_i_residual_value: CLEAR, and this is the condition that closed the route on three of the five names tried before it. Note 4.11 depreciates 'over the estimated useful lives' with nothing deducted - compare ADNOC Distribution's 'to allocate their cost TO THEIR RESIDUAL VALUES over their estimated useful lives' and Savola's 'depreciable amount represents cost of an asset ... LESS ITS RESIDUAL VALUE', both of which break the identity. The whole FY2025 document contains exactly three occurrences of 'residual value': the IAS 16 annual-review sentence at note 4.11, lease RESIDUAL VALUE GUARANTEES, and an investment-property VALUATION TECHNIQUE. No residual enters the depreciable amount and none is quantified anywhere.
STC.L328_condition_ii_reassessment: CLEAR, with AFFIRMATIVE evidence rather than an absence, and the affirmative evidence matters because the bands DID move. FY2023 disclosed Buildings 10 - 50 and Other assets 3 - 20; FY2024 and FY2025 disclose 25 - 50 and 2 - 20. The FY2024 filing footnotes both changed rows itself: '(*) Range has been updated to reflect the impact of deconsolidating discontinued operations (Note 14.1).' THAT IS A CHANGE IN THE POPULATION, NOT A REASSESSMENT OF ANY SURVIVING ASSET'S LIFE, which is the distinction this condition turns on - and it is the opposite of Savola, where four of five bands moved and the note asserted they had not. Note 5.2.2 carries only the standing sentence that asset lives are assessed annually; no change in accounting estimate is quantified anywhere for property and equipment.
STC.L328_condition_iii_business_combination: CLEAR. FY2025 acquisitions of new subsidiaries add SAR 9,898 thousand of cost against a base of 141,541,105 (0.007%) and 4,304 of accumulated depreciation against a charge of 6,453,343 (0.07%). Nothing resembling MODON's acquired history at thirty-four times the year's charge. The large FY2024 movement was a DISPOSAL of subsidiaries (note 14.1, cost -11,329,587 and accumulated -3,302,684), which removes both columns together; it is why that year's measured age steps only +0.58 rather than about +1.0, and it is outside the FY2025 year entirely.
STC.a_fourth_qualification_unquantified: Note 4.11 says 'MAINLY the straight-line method'. Both identities off this note - gross cost over the charge for the life, accumulated over the charge for the age - are exact only under straight line. The FY2025 document names no other depreciation method for property and equipment anywhere; every other straight-line sentence in it concerns leases, right-of-use assets or intangibles. So the exposure is small and undisclosed, its direction is unknown, and it is recorded rather than adjusted for.
STC.weighted_life_06-09-2026: THE RANGES WEIGHT TO A RANGE AND THAT ROUTE IS REFUSED; THE IDENTITY ROUTE IS OPEN BECAUSE ALL THREE CONDITIONS ABOVE ARE CLEAR. Weighting the three disclosed bands by the note's own amounts, capital-weighted HARMONIC (maintenance = sum of IC_class / L_class, so the aggregate life is the harmonic mean and not the arithmetic one): on depreciable GROSS COST of 134,634,729 the band runs 30.28 years with every class at its longest disclosed life to 3.21 years with every class at its shortest, a factor of 9.4; on NET BOOK VALUE of 36,379,959 it runs 30.81 to 3.37. A point inside that is this desk choosing a life under cover of a citation, so no single figure is recorded FROM THE BANDS. What IS recorded is the identity, below, which is a measurement off the same note's own columns rather than a choice.
STC.the_identity_per_class_06-09-2026: Depreciable gross cost over that class's OWN charge, FY2025: lands and buildings ex land 15,700,925 / 475,018 = 33.05 y (band 25-50, inside); telecommunication network and equipment 108,848,482 / 5,481,822 = 19.86 y (3-30, inside); OTHER ASSETS 10,085,322 / 496,503 = 20.31 y AGAINST A DISCLOSED MAXIMUM OF 20. That one breach is the only internal disagreement in the note and it is informative rather than fatal: it is what a largely-written-down base does to a cost-over-charge ratio, that class being 69.2% depreciated, and it says the identity reads marginally LONG - which under-states maintenance and over-states value. BOUNDED: capping that class at its own disclosed 20 years moves the pooled life from 20.863 to 20.838, -0.12%. The class is 7.49% of depreciable gross cost.
STC.the_pooled_identity_and_why_harmonic: 134,634,729 over 6,453,343 = 20.863 years, which IS the cost-weighted harmonic mean of the three class lives and reproduces the note's own charge by construction. The cost-weighted ARITHMETIC mean of the same three lives is 21.429 years and under-charges maintenance by SAR 170,654 thousand a year - 2.6% on the life, in the direction that flatters the value - so the distinction is not pedantry. Weights are GROSS COST rather than carrying amount deliberately: an asset 90% written down still costs full price to replace, so net book value is the wrong base for a replacement charge; both are shown above and differ by under 2% on the band.
STC.cross_check_prior_years: Three filed years hold the life inside 19.5 - 20.9, a 6.8% spread, and every table foots. FY2025 (FY2025 filing) 134,634,729 / 6,453,343 = 20.86 y, age 15.23 y, 73.0% depreciated. FY2024 as ORIGINALLY REPORTED (FY2024 filing) 130,697,817 / 6,600,613 = 19.80 y, age 14.37 y. FY2024 as RESTATED in the FY2025 comparative 130,697,817 / 6,690,097 = 19.54 y, age 14.18 y. FY2023 as originally reported (FY2023 filing) 135,611,856 / 6,834,977 = 19.84 y, age 13.60 y; as restated in the FY2024 comparative 136,217,457 / 6,834,977 = 19.93 y. THE FY2024 CHARGE IS FILED TWICE AT TWO VALUES and point-in-time discipline needs that recorded: the 89,484 difference is offset exactly in the transfers/reclassifications line (+67,242 against -22,242) and both routes reach the identical closing accumulated of 94,847,791, so it is a reclassification between two lines of one note rather than a restated charge; it moves that year's implied life by 1.3% and both sit inside the band. The measured age moves the way a year passing should: 13.60 -> 14.18 -> 15.23.
STC.the_cheap_cross_check_CANNOT_FIRE_HERE: terminal_value.py prescribes comparing the identity's implied life against the life the DISCLOSED CLASS RATES weight to, and on AIRARABIA that comparison fired at +48% and stopped a wrong number shipping. ON THIS NAME IT CANNOT FIRE: the disclosed band is 3.21 - 30.28 years and would contain almost any answer, so 20.86 sitting inside it is close to no evidence at all. What does the work here is the policy note read directly, which is the order terminal_value.py insists on - the note is the test and the arithmetic is a corroborator that works only sometimes.
STC.what_the_study_currently_commits: 20.862788 years, DERIVED BY IDENTITY and labelled as derived in its own terminal_record, which this reading reproduces exactly. WHAT THE LIFE ACTUALLY DOES IN THAT TERMINAL IS ALMOST NOTHING: the maintenance basis committed is book_dna_escalated over the MEASURED AGE of 15.225406 years (accumulated 98,254,770 over the charge 6,453,343, the same note, the same identity one column across), so the charge is 11,436.603 x 1.02^15.2254 = 15,461.02 and the life stands as the record and the corroborating cross-check rather than as a divisor. The cross-check between the two is CIRCULAR - one identity against another off the same two columns - which is why the policy-note reading above is what carries it.
STC.priced_across_the_band_06-09-2026: What the sanctioned terminal WOULD give, everything else held exactly as committed and the committed case reproduced bit-for-bit first (maintenance 15,461.02, TV 184,811.708 - identical to the study's own record, which is what makes the rest comparable): measured age 15.23 y gives TV 184,812; half the FY2025 identity life (10.43 y) 208,101 (+12.6%); half FY2024's 19.54 (9.77 y) 211,153 (+14.3%); half FY2023's 19.84 (9.92 y) 210,456 (+13.9%); the disclosed bands at their fast end (3.21 y, half 1.60) 245,606 (+32.9%) and at their slow end (30.28 y, half 15.14) 185,249 (+0.2%). THE DISCLOSED RANGES SPAN 33 POINTS OF TERMINAL VALUE, which is the whole argument for the identity, and the committed construction sits at the conservative end of every row. NOTHING HERE IS APPLIED AND NO PUBLISHED NUMBER MOVES - this is the size of the indeterminacy, not a correction, and the direction of any rebuild is not predicted either way per [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO CORRECTED].
STC.the_impairment_qualification: The note's line is 'Depreciation AND IMPAIRMENT' and no impairment figure for property and equipment is separately disclosed, so both identities carry whatever impairment sits inside the charge. Its direction is known: impairment inflates the denominator, which SHORTENS the life and the age, which UNDER-states the escalation to current cost, which UNDER-states maintenance and OVER-states value - so using the note's own column is the optimistic of the two available readings, and it is used because it is the column that foots. The charge series is smooth (6,834,977 -> 6,690,097 -> 6,453,343, changes of -2.1% and -3.5% on a base that grew), so no material impairment spike is visible; and the depreciated share of 73.0%, which has no charge in it at all, is what independently establishes that the base is old. Note 10(3) allocates 6,085,426 (2024: 6,205,009) of depreciation and impairment to operating cost lines from CONTINUING operations against the roll-forward's 6,453,343 and 6,690,097; that is not an impairment split - note 10(3) is also 'depreciation and impairment' - and it is not adopted for anything.
STC.negative_searches_actually_run: A disclosed depreciation RATE by class, which would pin a life outright the way EGCH's 3.95% does - none, this company discloses lives and not rates. A disclosed maintenance or sustaining capex, which would remove the need for a life at all - none in any filing held. A residual-value percentage by class - none, and note 4.11 deducts none. A quantified change in accounting estimate on property and equipment - none; the only band movement is the FY2024 deconsolidation footnote quoted above.
